### The failing line

- **line:** `M0-spec:28 N-17` — the ported validator's O rule (`tools/scaffold/m0-work.test.mjs:134-136`).
- **evidence:** the scaffold clause reads `(a.it.handsOver ?? []).some((h) => mentions(h, b.it.id))`: any hand-over
  line of M0-s-01 that names the receiver excuses every overlap between the scaffold and that receiver, whatever the
  path. The rule's own header says "or a path its `handsOver` names the receiver of", and C-0389 (5) states the port
  holds rule O. CONFIRMED: data mutant MW-O (M0-d-07 owns `plat/tools/landed/landed.mjs` too) leaves the test green;
  the checker's probe (`s4/probe/o-probe.mjs`, the test's own `workProblems`) gives `[]` for M0-d-07 taking
  `tools/landed/landed.mjs`, M0-d-03 taking `plat/package.json` and M0-k-05 taking `plat/vitest.config.ts`, while
  M0-a-02 (no hand-over) taking `tools/landed/landed.mjs` is named. Ten items are receivers in M0-s-01's `handsOver`.
  Under a flow label `landed` gives such a path to its latest owner, so an undeclared co-ownership the validator is
  meant to catch (N-17: "any edit to `owns` … is re-checked") would move the scaffold's file silently.
- **required change:** inside `tools/scaffold/m0-work.test.mjs`, let a scaffold hand-over excuse an overlap only when
  the hand-over line names the receiver **and** the path (for example: the line also contains the overlapping entry's
  path without `plat/`), keeping the `<module>` / `<harness>` clause; the checker's variant of exactly that
  (`s4/probe/m0-work-tight.test.mjs`) keeps the committed `M0-work.json` at 0 problem lines and names all three escapes
  above. Pin it with a planted break in the small work file (a receiver of a scaffold hand-over taking another scaffold
  path → one `O …` line), shown red on the current clause, and add the pin's mutant to the round's table.
